Emails are sent using the raw `guests` input, not `uniqueGuests`

`sendAddGuestsEmails` uses its `newGuests` argument to decide who gets the new-booking `AttendeeScheduledEmail` and who gets the "guests added" email (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:540-546). The handler passes the raw `guests` input, not the filtered `uniqueGuests` (line 74). If the input includes someone who is already an attendee, the handler filters them out and does not add them again, but they still get a fresh "new event scheduled" email instead of the update email. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

Server never de-duplicates the list or compares case-insensitively, so duplicate attendees get created and the blacklist can be bypassed

The server schema is just `z.array(z.string().email())` (addGuests.schema.ts:5). The uniqueness refine exists only in the dialog (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29), so an API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` makes two attendee rows through `createMany` (lines 92-106). The filter also compares exact strings. `guest === attendee.email` lets `A@x.com` be added next to an existing `a@x.com`. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased (line 71) but `guest` is not, so `Spam@blocked.com` gets past a `spam@blocked.com` entry. Lowercase the guests and de-duplicate them before filtering.

Any attendee can make the app email an unlimited list of arbitrary addresses

Matching on email alone lets any logged-in user whose email is on a booking (for example someone who booked a public event) add guests, and the guests array has no upper bound (addGuests.schema.ts:5). Every call sends the organizer, team members and every attendee an email from the app's mailer (email-manager.ts:525-549). That is a spam and amplification path. Consider capping `guests` with `.max(...)` and deciding whether attendees should have this permission at all.

A stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error stays after a successful add or after closing the dialog

`setIsInvalidEmail(false)` runs only in the Cancel handler (line 91). If a submit fails validation, the user corrects it and the add succeeds, `onSuccess` clears the emails but not `isInvalidEmail`, so the next time the dialog opens it shows the error at once. Closing with Esc or the overlay (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, line 61) also keeps the old emails and the old error. Reset both on success and whenever the dialog closes.

Error toast fallback can never run, and it can show 'undefined: …'

`message` is a template string and is never empty, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never uses the fallback. When `err.data` is missing (for example a network error), the toast reads `undefined: <raw message>`. Build the code prefix only when `err.data?.code` exists, and fall back to `unable_to_add_guests` when there is no message.

A backup code alone logs in without a password when any totpCode is sent too

The password is checked only when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new backup-code branch (line 131) runs whenever `backupCode` is set, and it never looks at `totpCode`. So a request to the credentials provider with `{ email, password: "", totpCode: "x", backupCode: <valid code> }` skips the password check, also gets past lines 113 and 117 for a CAL user who has a password, and then succeeds on the backup code. A leaked backup code is a static secret that often sits in the downloaded `cal-backup-codes.txt`, and it becomes enough to take over the account on its own. Before this change, the totpCode-skips-password path still needed a valid TOTP from the user's device. Fix: verify the password inside the backup-code branch, or make the line 121 condition `user.password && (!credentials.totpCode || credentials.backupCode)`. You could also reject requests that carry both `totpCode` and `backupCode`.

Closing the backup-codes step with Escape or an overlay click leaves the settings page saying 2FA is off

After a successful enable, `handleEnable` now moves to `DisplayBackupCodes` (line 135) instead of calling `onEnable()`. Only the Close button (lines 266-270) calls `onEnable`, which in turn calls `utils.viewer.me.invalidate()` (apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:65-67). If the dialog is dismissed through `onOpenChange` (Escape or a click outside), the parent only toggles `enableModalOpen` (two-factor-auth.tsx:64). The server already has `twoFactorEnabled: true`, but `me` is never refetched, so the switch still shows 2FA as disabled and nothing tells the user. `resetState()` is skipped as well, so the modal reopens on the backup-codes step. Fix: handle dismissal in this step by calling `onEnable`/`resetState` from the `onOpenChange` path, or block outside-dismiss while this step is shown.

Using up a backup code is read-modify-write, so the same code can work twice

The codes are read with the user (line 89), changed in memory, and written back without any condition (lines 149-156). Two logins running at the same time with the same code both find it at `indexOf` and both succeed, which breaks the promise in the locale text that each code works "exactly once". The per-email rate limit narrows the window but does not close it. An `updateMany` that matches the previous `backupCodes` ciphertext, plus a check on the affected row count, would make the step atomic.

`missing_backup_codes` points locked-out users to a settings page they cannot reach

This message appears on the login page (apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:158) for users who turned on 2FA before this feature existed. They have no backup codes, and by definition they cannot log in to reach settings. Even in settings there is no way to generate codes except disabling and re-enabling 2FA. Consider saying that no backup codes exist for the account and pointing to support, or to the TOTP/disable-and-re-enable path.

The default export of BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`

The component is copied from TwoFactor.tsx and keeps the name `TwoFactor`. In React DevTools and stack traces it then looks the same as the real `TwoFactor` component, which both login.tsx and DisableTwoFactorModal render next to it. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

Google Meet booking with no destination calendar throws TypeError

`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` gives `undefined` when the array is empty or null. `handleNewBooking` sends `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067), and the other callers send `[]`. When the location is Google Meet, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then throws, so the booking fails. Before this change the code fell back to Cal Video here. Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

Org slug condition is inverted

The old code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`: the slug was set right away only when billing is disabled, and when billing is enabled it was kept in `metadata.requestedSlug` until payment (features/ee/teams/api/upgrade.ts:45 publishes from `requestedSlug`). The new `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` flips this. With billing enabled, the org is published with its slug before anyone pays. With billing disabled (self-hosted), the org is created with no slug and no `requestedSlug`, so nothing can ever publish it. This rewrite is not part of the calendar change. Restore `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` on line 151.

Video references lose their credentialId

The old code saved `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results. Now it saves `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so every `_video` booking reference is stored without a credentialId. Later updates and deletes of the video meeting that look up the credential by `reference.credentialId` then fall back or fail. Keep `result.credentialId` for both kinds of result.

Non-Google calendars always write to the first host's calendar id

`EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now calls `createEvent(credential, event, ...)` once per host, each time with that host's credential and the full `destinationCalendar` array. Only Google uses the passed `credentialId` to pick its own entry. Office365 (this line), Lark (larkcalendar CalendarService.ts:128) and CalDAV (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-163) always take `destinationCalendar[0]`, which is the main host's calendar. A second collective host on Outlook gets a request to `/me/calendars/<host1 id>/events` under their own token, which fails. A CalDAV host's calendar list is filtered down to nothing. Either way the second host gets no event. Pick the entry whose `credentialId` matches the credential, as Google does, or use the `externalId` that `CalendarManager.createEvent` now receives.

updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback can never match

This branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, and then it looks for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, so it never finds a real calendar. Before, the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. In `updateEvent`, `calendarId` is now `undefined` and the Google API rejects the call. In `deleteEvent` (line 317) the code falls back to `primary`, which deletes from the wrong calendar. This hits references saved without `externalCalendarId`: older bookings, and, after this PR, every event created through the no-credentialId path in `createAllCalendarEvents` (EventManager.ts:376-381), because `createEvent` is called there without an `externalId`. Fall back to the destination calendar whose `credentialId` matches this credential, or to the first entry.

Team members' calendars are dropped when the organizer has none

If neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (line 1067). `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then does nothing, so the other collective hosts' calendars are thrown away without any sign. Initialise it to `[]` and push into that.

Recurring cancellation repeats per reference and skips other hosts

The recurring branch now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. For every calendar reference it goes through all of the organizer's calendar credentials and deletes `updBooking.references.find(...)`, which is always the first calendar reference. With N host references, the organizer's event is deleted N times, and the other hosts' recurring events are never deleted, because only `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` is used and only the first ref of each booking is looked at. Run the recurring deletion once, outside the loop, over every `_calendar` reference of each booking, using each reference's own credential.

Member calendars without credentialId end up on the organizer's credentials

When a pushed team member's `destinationCalendar` has no `credentialId`, `createAllCalendarEvents` takes the else branch (EventManager.ts:376-381). That branch filters `this.calendarCredentials`, which are the organizer's credentials, by integration type, so it creates a second copy of the event in the organizer's calendar instead of the member's. Consider skipping such entries for non-organizer hosts, or resolving that member's credentials.

loadUsers turns validation errors into a 500

An empty `dynamicUserList` now throws a plain `Error`. The catch block turns that into `HttpError(500, "Unable to load users")`, while before the code returned an empty list and handled it downstream. `error instanceof HttpError` can never be true inside this try block. Also, the `organization.slug` select was removed from the dynamic-user query, but `IsFixedAwareUser` (line 355) still declares it.

The `import()` calls run as soon as the module loads, so nothing is loaded lazily

Every property in this object literal is an `import("./x")` expression. Each one is evaluated, and starts loading its app, at the moment `@calcom/app-store` is first imported. All 28 apps still load on every cold start, whether or not the request uses them. The only difference from the static imports is that callers now have to `await`. To defer loading until an app is actually requested, store thunks instead (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and call them at the lookup sites: `getCalendar.ts:15`, `videoClient.ts:26`, `handlePayment.ts:26`, `deletePayment.ts:16`, `handleCancelBooking.ts:589` and `bookings.tsx:967`. A side effect of the eager version: an app module that fails to load produces a rejected promise that nothing handles until some request happens to look that app up.

`forEach(async …)` means the surrounding try/catch no longer catches errors from `getCalendar`

`getCalendar` is now async. Before, an exception thrown while building the CalendarService (inside `getCalendar`) was synchronous and reached the `catch` at line 135, which logged it. Now it rejects the promise returned by the async `forEach` callback, and that promise is discarded. The `catch` cannot see it, so the error becomes an unhandled rejection and is never logged through `logger`. The same pattern is in `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125` and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553`; in bookings.tsx there is no try/catch at all. The `deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting` promises were already fire-and-forget before this change. Collecting the promises with `map` and putting `await Promise.allSettled(...)` inside the try would restore the logging and also wait for the deletions before the reschedule emails are sent.

Account UI message switched from i18next `{{n}}` placeholders to MessageFormat syntax that i18next won't interpolate

This bundle is loaded by i18next, and `js/apps/account-ui/src/i18n.ts:27-29` sets no custom interpolation prefix, so the default `{{ }}` delimiters apply. Every sibling error message in this file uses `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, `{{2}}` (lines 14, 27, 29, 36, 37). The new value uses `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and a Java `{2,choice,...}` pattern, and i18next interpolates none of these. A user who breaks a multivalued size constraint in the Account Console would see the literal text `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` The same change is in `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties:3138`, so the Admin Console has the same problem. Keep the `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` form for the two React bundles, for example `... at most {{2}} value(s).`, or use i18next plurals. Apply the MessageFormat `choice` form only to the server-rendered themes. I did not read the ui-shared code that passes `error.params` to `t()`, which is why confidence is medium.

Admin UI message now uses MessageFormat placeholders that i18next won't substitute

This is the same problem as in the account-ui bundle. The old value used the i18next `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` placeholders, which the React admin console interpolates. The new value uses `{0}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`, which i18next leaves as literal text, so admins would see raw placeholders in the validation error. Keep i18next syntax in this bundle.

Anchor violation message names neither the key nor the file

`ThemeVerifierMojo` collects the messages from every scanned properties file into one list and throws `MojoFailureException("Validation errors: " + messages)` (`misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/ThemeVerifierMojo.java:51-55`). The duplicate-key message (line 194) and the illegal-HTML message (line 111) both include the file, and the HTML one includes the key. This message has only the tag, so with dozens of locale files a failing build gives no clue which translation to fix. Add `key` (the parameter is already passed in but never used) and `file` to the message.

ANCHOR_PATTERN also matches `<abbr>`, `<area>`, `<audio>`, `<address>` …

`</?a[^>]*>` matches any tag whose name starts with `a`. Nothing unsafe gets through: an unmatched tag is still reported. But a translation containing `<abbr>` or `<audio …>` is reported as "Didn't find anchor tag" instead of as illegal HTML, which is misleading. `</?a(\s[^>]*)?>` limits the match to real anchors.

Missing English counterpart aborts the build with a RuntimeException

Line 74 derives the English file path by string rewriting. If a scanned messages file has no `_en` sibling at that path (a theme that only ships translations, or a different directory layout), `verifySafeHtml` throws an unchecked `RuntimeException`. The mojo does not catch it, so it ends the build with a stack trace and no aggregated report. `verify()` already converts I/O errors to `MojoExecutionException`. Either do the same here, or fall back to treating every English value as "no HTML".

Codes regenerated into user storage leave the old local codes valid

When `updateCredential` succeeds in user storage, the code returns without touching any `recovery-authn-codes` credential already in the local DB. Only the `else` branch goes through `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential`, which deletes the old stored credential first (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:39-42).

At login, `UserCredentialManager.isValid` asks the federated validator first. If that validator rejects the input, the input stays in `toValidate` and the local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` checks it against the stale local codes (UserCredentialManager.java:66-79, 270-278).

When it happens: a federated user who set up recovery codes before their provider supported the type, then regenerates them. Their old codes still log them in, and nothing tells them. Fix: in the `userStorageCreated` branch, remove any stored local recovery-codes credential.

Federated recovery codes are never consumed, and the cleanup goes to the wrong store

For a local credential, `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid` removes the used code and saves the change (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:109-112). The federated path has no matching step.

`getCredential` now returns the user-storage credential, but the authenticator never tells user storage that a code was used. When `allCodesUsed()` is true, it calls `removeStoredCredentialById` with the federated credential's id, and that call goes to the local store (UserCredentialManager.java:114-117), so the federated credential is never removed.

The test provider shows the effect: `isValid` accepts any code in the list and never removes it (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:326-340). The same code can be reused forever, and the login page always asks for code #1. The SPI says nothing about who consumes the code.

Fix: either define that contract (for example, call `updateCredential`/`disableCredentialType` on user storage when codes run out) or document that the provider must consume codes. Also make the test provider do it.

Overriding getCredentials (and returning OTP) defeats the purpose of the 4.8.3 compatibility provider

The class Javadoc says this provider stands for code written for Keycloak 4.8.3 that "should work fine without a need to change the code" (lines 59-60). The new `getCredentials` override, which did not exist then, now also returns the OTP model.

Before this change, the default `getCredentials` returned an empty stream (CredentialInputUpdater.java:50-51). The existing OTP account-REST tests therefore covered the fallback in AccountCredentialResource.java:212-217, which builds a dummy credential with an `otp-id` placeholder id, and the `-id` branch in CredentialDeleteHelper.java:75-79. They now go through the real-model path at CredentialDeleteHelper.java:64 instead, so the legacy behaviour has no test left.

Keep OTP out of `getCredentials`, or put recovery-code support in a separate, modern test provider.

Federated recovery credential has no id and cannot be disabled

`createFromValues` never sets an id (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:58-85), and the generated `recoveryCodes.getId()` is thrown away. The account REST API therefore lists the credential with a null id. `CredentialDeleteHelper` cannot match it (line 64), and `disableCredentialType`/`getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` ignore recovery codes (lines 217-224, 255-263), so the credential cannot be removed from the account console.

`getMyUser(user)` can also return null here, which throws a NullPointerException; `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` checks for null. Set the id from `myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()` and add null checks.

Test never checks that a used code is rejected or that the next code is requested

`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` logs in once with code 0 and stops. A second login that expects code 1, or a check that reusing code 0 fails, would have caught the missing consumption on the federated path. The delayed-authenticator step with delay 0 does nothing, and its alias has a typo (`delayed-suthenticator-config`, line 135).

Hard-coded provider id; provider is looked up even when it is not used

`"keycloak-recovery-authn-codes"` repeats `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.java:11). If that constant changes, `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider` silently becomes null and line 129 throws a NullPointerException. Use the constant if the module can see it, or look the provider up only in the `else` branch.

Operator guide says the Operator fails without `rolling-updates`, but no Operator code checks the feature

The new caution says the Operator "will fail" if `rolling-updates` is not enabled. Nothing under `operator/src/main` mentions `rolling-updates` or `ROLLING_UPDATES`. The upgrade logic picks `RecreateOnImageChangeUpgradeLogic` or `AlwaysRecreateUpgradeLogic` (`operator/src/main/java/org/keycloak/operator/upgrade/UpgradeLogicFactory.java:38-41`) without looking at features, and `features.enabled` is only passed through as the `--features` server option (`KeycloakDistConfigurator.java:122-124`). The PR's own `UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment` deploys without the feature when the strategy is unset (`UpgradeTest.java:105-106`), and the test still expects the upgrade to work. Either reword the caution to describe what actually needs the feature (the `update-compatibility` commands inside the server image), or add the Operator-side check it describes.

Hard-coded `--features=rolling-updates` replaces a user's own feature list for the command

The macro now always ends the command with `--features=rolling-updates`. Users who already turn on other features with `--features` or `KC_FEATURES` will copy this line as written. The CLI value then wins over their configured list, so the metadata/check run uses a different feature set from the real deployment. That goes against the guide's own warning to include every configuration option (`update-compatibility.adoc:70-75`, `87-91`). It does no harm today, because the check only compares versions. It will produce wrong results once features are compared. Consider telling users to add `rolling-updates` to their existing `--features` list instead of appending a separate flag.

Exit-code remap (recreate 4→3, new 4 = feature disabled) has no test

This change moves `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and gives 4 a new meaning, feature disabled. The guide tells automation to rely only on these exit codes (`update-compatibility.adoc:55`). No test checks either value: `UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled` only checks the error message, and `testWrongVersions` only checks stderr text (`UpdateCommandDistTest.java:48-50`, `96-106`). Adding `assertEquals(4, ...)` and `assertEquals(3, result.exitCode())` would stop the codes from drifting away from the documented table, which is how 4 and 3 got mixed up before this PR.
